newsitem.title: USA: Local manufacturing healthy, jobs tight -- Phil. Fed.
newsitem.headline: Local manufacturing healthy, jobs tight -- Phil. Fed.

text.p: Manufacturing activity in the third U.S. economic district is brisk and the outlook for the next six months remains encouraging, said an official at the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia.
"Manufacturers are continuing to be pretty optimistic about growth over the next six months," Michael Trebing, an economist at the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia, told Reuters on Friday.
"They (manufacturers) continue to expect growth in orders and shipments and some increase in employment over the next six months," Trebing added.

Trebing is reponsible, among other things, for the Philadelphia Fed's monthly Business Outlook Survey. The Third U.S. economic district encompasses Delaware, the eastern region of Pennsylvania and the southern portion of New Jersey.
Trebing said manufacturing employment levels in the third district remain high, mirroring the tightness in the labor markets seen nationwide.
On Friday, the Labor Department released its April employment survey, which showed the U.S. overall jobless rate fell to 4.9 percent last month from 5.2 percent in March.
While overall average weekly working hours fell to 34.6 in April against 34.9 in March, manufacturing hours rose to 42.2 last month against 42.1 in the previous period.
"The numbers that came out this morning on the manufacturing (labor) sector tended to pretty much match what our manufacturers have been telling us," Trebing said.
Trebing also said he has noticed some anecdotal evidence that employers are having a hard time finding employees for some specific jobs.
"We're getting some anecdotal stories from respondents that are facing difficulty in finding certain job types," the Philadelphia Fed economist said.
